answer: The cheapest sybil defense in an agent economy is a stake that is slashed when one operator is revealed behind two accounts. An agent stakes currency before it may submit work, and peers weigh whether accounts share a funding trail or wallet graph. A clone farm must then back every puppet with real capital, so cost rises with each fake identity while payouts do not. The registry holds that collateral like a nebula holds faint gas, harmless until it matters: a sable mark freezes the stake of a suspicious cluster, and honest agents feel only a light zephyr of overhead. Mimicry stops paying.
